problem_statement: The conversion routines between Zephyr k_timeout_t timeouts and POSIX struct timespec durations produce incorrect or unsafe results for several durations. Converting a duration to ticks and back must round up to the next tick boundary for any non-zero finite duration that fits within the maximum representable tick count, round down to the maximum representable tick count for durations above that boundary (keeping finite durations finite rather than collapsing them to K_FOREVER), map the maximum representable timespec to K_FOREVER, and treat non-positive or negative durations as K_NO_WAIT. The conversion that produces the remainder must report the difference between the requested and converted durations. Converting a negative (absolute) timeout must be rejected rather than silently accepted, and normalizing/adding/negating/overflowing timespecs must be correct for any supported width of the time field. The expected durations for a fixed tick rate (e.g. the maximum representable timespec and its remainder) must match the documented semantics.

verification.reason: The statement describes the required behaviour well but omits the exact names of 12 new public macros that the tests reference directly, and does not state the new two-argument signature of timespec_to_timeout. All of these are public interface details that can be added to the statement without revealing implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden tests use the macro names SYS_TIME_T_MAX, SYS_TIME_T_MIN, K_TICK_MIN, K_TICK_MAX, SYS_TICKS_TO_SECS, SYS_TICKS_TO_NSECS, SYS_TICKS_TO_TIMESPEC, SYS_TIMESPEC, SYS_TIMESPEC_NO_WAIT, SYS_TIMESPEC_MIN, SYS_TIMESPEC_MAX, and SYS_TIMESPEC_FOREVER directly, but the problem statement never mentions any of these names. The agent cannot guess them.

The hidden tests call timespec_to_timeout with two arguments (e.g. timespec_to_timeout(&tspec->tspec, &rem)), but the problem statement only describes the behaviour of the remainder without stating the new two-parameter signature (const struct timespec *req, struct timespec *rem).

The tests rely on SYS_TIMESPEC performing clamping of tv_sec to [SYS_TIME_T_MIN, SYS_TIME_T_MAX] (e.g. SYS_TIMESPEC(0, NSEC_PER_USEC) constructs a valid timespec), and on SYS_TIMESPEC_NO_WAIT being the timespec equivalent of K_NO_WAIT (0,0) used in comparisons. The statement does not describe these interface properties.

leak_check.leak_detail: The clause 'using SYS_TICKS_TO_SECS and SYS_TICKS_TO_NSECS' hints at the implementation of a public macro, but the rest is public interface/behavior; this is minor.
leak_check.suggested_statement:
The conversion routines between Zephyr k_timeout_t timeouts and POSIX struct timespec durations produce incorrect or unsafe results for several durations. The following macros must be defined in include/zephyr/sys/timeutil.h: SYS_TIME_T_MAX and SYS_TIME_T_MIN (the maximum and minimum values representable by the time_t type); K_TICK_MIN (the minimum positive tick duration, equal to 1) and K_TICK_MAX (the maximum representable finite tick count, equal to INT64_MAX when CONFIG_TIMEOUT_64BIT is set and UINT32_MAX - 1 otherwise); SYS_TICKS_TO_SECS(ticks) (converts a tick count to seconds, discarding any fractional part, mapping K_TICKS_FOREVER to SYS_TIME_T_MAX); SYS_TICKS_TO_NSECS(ticks) (converts a tick count to nanoseconds modulo NSEC_PER_SEC, mapping K_TICKS_FOREVER to NSEC_PER_SEC - 1); SYS_TICKS_TO_TIMESPEC(ticks) (converts a tick count to a struct timespec with the corresponding seconds and nanoseconds components); SYS_TIMESPEC(sec, nsec) (constructs a struct timespec from seconds and nanoseconds, clamping tv_sec to the range [SYS_TIME_T_MIN, SYS_TIME_T_MAX]); SYS_TIMESPEC_NO_WAIT (the timespec equivalent of K_NO_WAIT, i.e. {0, 0}); SYS_TIMESPEC_MIN (the timespec equivalent of K_TICK_MIN); SYS_TIMESPEC_MAX (the timespec equivalent of K_TICK_MAX); and SYS_TIMESPEC_FOREVER (the timespec equivalent of K_FOREVER, defined as {SYS_TIME_T_MAX, NSEC_PER_SEC - 1}).

Converting a duration to ticks and back must round up to the next tick boundary for any non-zero finite duration that fits within the maximum representable tick count, round down to the maximum representable tick count for durations above that boundary (keeping finite durations finite rather than collapsing them to K_FOREVER), map the maximum representable timespec (SYS_TIMESPEC_MAX) to K_FOREVER, and treat non-positive or negative durations as K_NO_WAIT. The function timespec_to_timeout must accept an optional second parameter of type struct timespec * (the remainder, which may be NULL); when non-NULL it must be set to the difference between the requested duration and the converted duration, i.e. requested minus converted. Converting a negative (absolute) timeout in timespec_from_timeout must assert rather than silently accept it, and normalizing/adding/negating/overflowing timespecs must be correct for any supported width of the time field. The expected durations for a fixed tick rate (e.g. the maximum representable timespec and its remainder) must match the documented semantics.
